# After each joint: what must read zero, and what must not

`canfuel/docs/install.md` step 5 has you measure every part **before** it
goes in, which catches a misread colour code and nothing else. This is the
other half, and it is per **joint** rather than per part.

A soldered joint fails in two directions and neither one is visible:

- **open** — the iron never wetted the pad, or the lead moved as it cooled
- **bridged** — solder reached the nearest copper, which is hardly ever the
  next pad along

So every pad gets two readings. **Continuity** proves the joint exists;
**isolation** proves nothing else got caught. Look the second one up rather
than guessing it — SGND is poured on both layers, so for most pads the
nearest copper is ground, a fraction of a millimetre away, on every side.

## How to hold the meter

- **Continuity (beeper) for the "zero" column.** A joint either rings or
  it does not.
- **Resistance, not the beeper, for anything with a capacitor across it.**
  A 10 µF part charges through the meter, so the beeper chirps once and
  goes quiet. That chirp is the capacitor, not a bridge. Watch the number
  climb instead: it must settle in megohms or `OL`. A steady near-zero that
  never moves is a bridge.
- **Measure with nothing else fitted yet**, which is what the solder order
  in install.md gives you for free. Once the neighbours are in, every
  reading is of whatever else shares the net.
- **The distances below are copper edge to copper edge, as designed.**
  Solder mask sits between most of them, which makes a bridge less likely
  and not impossible. Anything under about 0.6 mm is worth the ten
  seconds.

## How to read it

Find the part you have just soldered. Every one of its pads gets a row.

- **`—` in the zero column** means the pad is on no net. Fourteen of U1's
  pins are like that: the pin goes nowhere and there is nothing it should
  ring to. Its **open** column still matters — the firmware drives every
  unused pin low, so a bridge from one of them to +5 V is a short through
  the port driver.
- **U1 and U2 are the socket holes**, so their rows are checked once the
  socket is soldered and before either chip goes in. That is also the only
  time the holes are reachable.
- **A named probe point is a hole you can find by eye** — `J3 pin 1` is the
  square pad of the ICSP header, `U1 pin 1` the end the silk notch marks.
  Where several are listed, any of them will do.

| Pad | Net | Must read **zero** to | Must stay **open** to |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | OSC1 | U1 pin 9, Y1 pad 1 | **SGND** 0.30 mm (any ground — J3 pin 3) |
| 2 | SGND | any ground — J3 pin 3 | nothing within 1.0 mm |
